framing: A response can read smoothly, cite a real document, and still fabricate the critical detail
paragraphs: When a documentation assistant answers a question about PyTorch compiler behavior, it may retrieve the exact page for custom autograd functions, quote a valid version header, and then append a confident sentence claiming that fullgraph=True silently falls back to eager execution on Python hooks. In fact, the retrieved chunk states the opposite: fullgraph=True raises an error on graph breaks, while silent fallback belongs to fullgraph=False. Evaluating the reply as a single aggregate block allows surface fluency and one valid citation to mask a direct contradiction.

Detecting hallucinations requires separating two questions that evaluations often collapse: whether a statement is faithful to retrieved context, and whether it is accurate in the wider world. A claim can copy an outdated index chunk verbatim, or state a generally true fact from model weights without any support in the prompt context. Decomposing generated prose into atomic claims turns holistic grading into structured verification, letting a system separate grounded statements from missing evidence and direct contradictions.

This chapter builds detection and verification signals from the ground up using token predictive entropy, sequence perplexity, multi-sample semantic consistency, and calibrated natural language inference scoring. You will measure where uncertainty and multi-sample consensus catch spontaneous fabrications, see why shared parametric misconceptions still pass agreement checks confidently, and trace precision-recall and conformal risk-coverage curves to govern abstention thresholds.

Earlier chapters examined counterfactual fairness across prompt slices and retrieval evaluation. Here, you convert per-claim support scores into concrete routing actions: serve intact, prune unsupported clauses, trigger corrective retrieval, or abstain. In the following chapter on observability and monitoring, those claim-level scores, pruned counts, and abstention decisions become live traces for diagnosing silent quality degradation.
outcomes: Decompose model outputs into atomic claims and separate context faithfulness from world accuracy.
Evaluate token entropy, perplexity, and multi-sample semantic consistency alongside NLI verification.
Calibrate verifier scores and set conformal abstention thresholds along empirical risk-coverage curves.
question: When can a pipeline safely prune an unsupported clause and serve the rest, and when must it retrieve fresh context or abstain?
